messages.subject: Estimated D = N ?
parts:
Hi All
I am using DISTANCE to estimate primate populations observed using line transects. When entering my data DISTANCE estimates my Density of animals (D = animals/km2) as equal to  the number of animals in specific area (N). I have a hard time believing this as my sampled area is not equal to 1 km2. Do anyone have advice to what I am doing wrong? I dit not get this problem a few months back, last time I worked with DISTANCE. 

Thank you 
Laerke Johansen

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Estimated D = N ?
parts:
Lærke

Difficult to know what the problem might be.  Distance simply multiplies the density it computes by the area of the strata or study region you have provided.  What values did you provide in the field "area" associated with the study area layer (if you had no strata) or the region layer (if you stratified your study area)?
